burst.interpretation: Four leader admissions, four coalesced cache reads and eight normal cache hits were observed. Total object GETs were four; auth used thirteen KV reads. Sharing is per isolate and concurrent requests can also arrive after a fill completes. This result does not prove one global fill or cached auth for every burst execution.

cpuEvidence.platformPhaseMetrics: Collected separately by the metrics agent; exact intervals and planned counts are in windows. Adaptive sample intervals must be retained.

findings: All 109 calls succeeded. All 100 full Base64 JSON results match the saved independent reference and the live same-block results. The four complete binary bodies match the original V1 bundle SHA-256 values.
Plain cold JSON is still slower than Helius. The optimized p50 was 201.444 ms, compared with 204.109 ms for the unchanged native Worker and 114.054 ms for Helius in the same phase.

Hinted server-cold JSON uses the same three object GETs and a KV read, with all owner application caches bypassed. Its p50 was 162.114 ms, compared with Helius at 105.586 ms in that phase. Prior locator downloads are a separate cost.
Source-only JSON proves cached index and two source GETs in all four calls. Auth was cached in three calls; the other call used one KV read. Source-only is not fully cold.
All sixteen measured response hits used zero object GETs. Their p50 was 52.512 ms, compared with Helius at 94.544 ms. Their p95 was 230.392 ms, compared with Helius at 149.215 ms.

The slowest response HIT used a reused socket, Auth HIT/KV0 and zero source reads. Headers arrived at 21.028 ms; the compressed entity transfer took 201.400 ms. This tail is not an observed origin read or a client reconnect.

The concurrent burst passed all sixteen full JSON parity checks. It used four GETs, four LEADER receipts, four COALESCED receipts and eight ordinary HIT receipts. One resolution/auth warm request did not guarantee an auth HIT in each burst execution; thirteen KV reads occurred.

Earlier and later phases have different runtime, service-cache and network histories. The phase latency difference alone does not prove a causal speedup from locator hints. Per-request stage, storage and transport evidence is preserved.
limits: The sample uses four fixed blocks from one epoch and one client location. p95 and p99 are the largest value for groups with eight or fewer calls. It does not show a global provider ranking.
Full cold bypasses owner caches only. Cloudflare physical storage and service cache state, and Helius cache state, remain unknown.
The final deployment uses a fresh archive/response generation. No root smoke request preceded this run, and the instrumented diagnostic used a different version and cache generation.

A persistent per-origin dispatcher was used. The fast pool allowed sixteen connections for the concurrent burst; first socket setup and reuse remain visible in the raw trace. A numeric diagnostic header was sent to all targets and does not change the Worker canonical cache key.
Burst JSON validation ran after all response bodies completed. Its local validation time is outside the network phase. No per-request client CPU is attributed during concurrent work.
Worker profile clocks can remain unchanged during synchronous work. Zero decode/render milliseconds do not mean zero CPU. CPU cost must come from separate platform evidence.

Binary source byte counters are snapshots at response headers. The expected streamed byte count is separate from actual buffered bytes. Exact binary parity proves complete delivery but is not a final backend byte receipt.
The new and unchanged native Workers use the same full source objects, original offsets and source ETags. No archive or resolution object was copied by the benchmark.
No retry, post-run probe or extra data request was made. Locator tokens and credentials are absent from public reports.
